PullRequest.Title: agentHost: route offered client tools before replacement settles
PullRequest.Body:

### Context

Follow-up to #343980. The runtime can start a newly offered client tool after accepting `setTools` but before the response reaches the host. Routing was only committed after the response, so that start had no client contributor and its handler could wait forever when no permission callback occurred.

### Change

Stage routing *before* replacing tools rather than holding calls until it settles:

- While `replaceTools` is in flight, `_clientToolNames` is the union of applied and offered client tool names, and `_resolveClientToolOwner` prefers the offered definition (so same-name contract changes route to the client that provides the new definition).
- On success, the offered set is committed as before. On rejection, the applied routing is restored and the error propagates to the caller.

The union is safe because every reader looks up a name the runtime actually invoked, and each call captures its contributor when it starts. A rejected replacement never offered the new tools, so no calls to them can exist. Existing calls and unchanged tools are unaffected.

### Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts`: passed (1,379).
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts`: passed (940).
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts`: passed.
- With the source change reverted, both new/updated tests fail: a handler timeout for the in-flight call, and a wrong contributor for the same-name contract change.
- Repository precommit hygiene: passed.

The tests cover a start and handler completing during an in-flight replacement without a permission callback, retained routing after a rejected replacement, and same-name contract changes routing to the client with the new definition. Full integration and smoke suites were not run.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A newly offered client-tool handler could park a DeferredPromise in PendingRequestRegistry during the asynchronous setTools boundary while routing still reflected only the old snapshot. Because the emitted start lacked a client contributor, no client response resolved it, blocking the tool invocation and turn indefinitely and retaining the pending entry until session cleanup.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: A client tool invoked in the narrow setTools acceptance window could hang the active agent turn indefinitely, with one pending deferred retained per affected invocation until the session ended.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The fix stages the union of applied/offered client names and the offered definitions before awaiting replaceTools, so an invocation started by the runtime during that boundary is attributed to the providing client and its pending handler receives a completion; rejection restores the prior routing.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, updateClientTools awaited configuration.replaceTools/session.setTools at line 3695 before updating _clientToolNames and _appliedSnapshot. The runtime can invoke a newly supplied Tool handler while setTools is still pending: the handler calls _pendingClientToolCalls.register(toolCallId), while tool.execution_start attribution uses _clientToolNames and _appliedSnapshot through _getToolCallContributor/_resolveClientToolOwner. With the old post-await state, the start had no client contributor, so no client completion was produced and the PendingRequestRegistry entry remained parked until session teardown. The changed test exercises exactly this ordering and awaits the handler before releasing the setTools gate.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refreshing a live or pre-warmed Copilot session after the active client's tool definitions change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before a send/resume can proceed with a changed snapshot, updateClientTools builds the SDK tool list and awaits replaceTools/session.setTools. The diff only stages in-memory routing before that existing await; no new boundary is added to the send critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Replace the runtime's complete SDK tool list through session.setTools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per structurally changed tool snapshot; identical snapshots short-circuit before the boundary. A rejected update can be retried once by a later refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single setTools request was issued and awaited, but client routing was updated only after it resolved.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request is awaited before the refreshed send/resume continues; the new Set union and offered-definition reference are synchronous staging immediately before the same await.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of offered/applied client tool definitions controls the temporary Set construction and existing SDK payload size. Work remains linear once per changed snapshot rather than per tool boundary call.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Production callers reach refresh through the per-chat Sequencer, so replacements for one chat are serialized. The SDK runtime may nevertheless begin an offered tool while the single setTools request is in flight; this overlap is the behavior handled by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: _appliedSnapshot provides a warm-state equality guard: unchanged definitions issue no setTools call. Successful changes commit the new snapshot; failures restore routing and are not negatively cached, allowing an explicit retry. Production per-chat sequencing prevents duplicate same-chat refreshes from racing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the caller queues, equality guard, one replaceTools await, and staged in-memory assignments are directly visible in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The maximum extension-contributed tool count and duration of the SDK setTools IPC are not measured here, but the diff does not increase IPC count or payload cardinality and adds only one bounded linear Set construction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Boundary cardinality and critical-path placement are unchanged, while the added allocation is bounded by the already-serialized tool-list update.

Scenarios.Scenario: A newly offered client tool starts executing before the SDK setTools response reaches the host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The runtime emits tool.execution_start and invokes the supplied handler during the in-flight replacement. Correct attribution must synchronously route the start to the owning client; the handler then waits for the client's completion. Before this fix, missing staged routing left the PendingRequestRegistry promise unresolved until session teardown, blocking the tool call and active turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The in-flight session.setTools request causes the runtime to accept and potentially invoke the newly offered handler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One replacement IPC for the changed snapshot, regardless of how many tools are in the snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The runtime could already invoke an offered handler before setTools settled, but host routing still used only the applied snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Its response is not required before the newly offered handler can start, which creates the race addressed by staged routing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the attributed client-tool start to the owning client and receive its completion back into the pending registry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One start/completion round trip per actual client-tool invocation; ownership lookup is in-memory and no extra boundary call is made per candidate client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Normal applied client tools used this round trip, but a newly offered tool in the setTools window was emitted without a client contributor, so no completion arrived and its deferred remained parked.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The completion resolves the SDK handler and lets the active turn continue. The diff restores this existing round trip for invocations occurring during replacement.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with actual tool invocations during the short replacement window, not with every definition. Ownership lookup scans the offered definition list and active clients once per such start; this replaces the prior applied-list scan and is bounded by configured tools/clients.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The replacement itself is one per-chat serialized operation, but the runtime can overlap one or more model-issued tool invocations with it. Each invocation captures its contributor and has its own toolCallId/deferred; the diff does not add parallel SDK requests or remove backpressure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no result cache for tool execution. The offered routing state exists only until setTools settles; success commits it, rejection restores the applied name set, and each invocation retains its captured contributor. Pending results are keyed by toolCallId and removed on response or session cleanup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the handler registers a DeferredPromise, the client response is the only normal resolver, the old routing commit occurred after await, and the changed test completes the handler before releasing the setTools gate.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The race frequency and number of parallel model tool calls are workload-dependent, but the old indefinite wait and the fixed call path are directly demonstrated. The diff's additional lookup/temporary state is short-lived and bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced performance regression. This PR fixes a concrete latency/cleanup regression by making the existing client completion path reachable during the SDK acceptance window; the fix was recorded with its blamed introducer.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Traced tool-refresh sequencing, setTools IPC cardinality, routing lookup cost, failure rollback, pending-request cleanup, and the in-flight invocation race. No actionable performance regression was introduced; the PR fixes an indefinite pending client-tool handler regression and adds only bounded in-memory staging.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
